chunks.arabic_text: وَبِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ

translations.en: And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَنْ سَاءَتْهُ سَيِّئَةٌ وَ سَرَّتْهُ حَسَنَةٌ فَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ

translations.en: He who is displeased by his evil deed and pleased by his good deed, then he is a believer.

en.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to distinguish the psychological state of the *Mu'min* from mere ritual compliance, emphasizing that true faith manifests in emotional responsiveness to one's deeds. This aligns with the Shia concept of *Fitrah*, where the believer's innate nature recoils from sin and embraces virtue, serving as a continuous internal barometer of spiritual health. The narration underscores that self-awareness and emotional sincerity are integral to the definition of belief in Shia theology.
en.seo_question: What is the defining characteristic of a believer according to this hadith?
